title: Maple Leafs sign Jack Roslovic to 2-year deal
content:
The Maple Leafs have signed forward Jack Roslovic to a two-year contract with a cap hit of $4 million, according to league sources speaking on the condition of anonymity to address negotiations that aren’t public.

The 29-year-old has scored 20 goals in each of the past two seasons and brings some skill to the Leafs’ forward group.

Roslovic looks likely to join the top six in Toronto next season, perhaps even alongside Auston Matthews on the team’s top line. He was a teammate of Matthews with the U.S. National Development Team Program.

Roslovic has struggled to produce in the playoffs. He managed just one assist and no goals in six games for the Oilers last spring, playing just 13 minutes a game. He was a healthy scratch at times the previous spring for Carolina, scoring just once in nine games while adding three assists.

Roslovic has registered three goals and 18 points in 51 career playoff games.

The Leafs effectively picked Roslovic over Matias Maccelli, who wasn’t issued a qualifying offer of $4.1 million on Monday, making him a free agent. Maccelli signed a one-year deal worth $2.25 million with the Islanders on Wednesday.
